title: That five year clause? Meet reality

 That five year clause? Meet reality
Hi Sara,
Here’s a fun surprise I see way too often:
A non-compete that says, “No competing for five years from closing.”
Sounds strong. Looks good on paper.
And still leaves a massive hole.
Because if the seller sticks around helping during tax season, even casually, they’re still in front of the clients. Still in the loop. Still part of the important client relationships.
Then five years pass. The non-compete ends.

And now they can walk out the door with the very clients they never stopped talking to.
Legally.
Here’s what I do instead:
Write the non-compete to last five years from closing and two years after the seller stops working with the buyer.
That simple phrase can save your whole deal.
If you’re buying a business and the non-compete doesn’t match the way people actually behave, you’re not protected. You’re just optimistic.
And while you’re at it, slip in a non-disparagement because, trust me.
Want more of the details buyers miss until it's too late?
Check out my YouTube channel, DealMakers, for real talk on structuring smart transactions.
To smarter deals that actually hold,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder of Deal Academy
